positive.prompt: Promote this approved idea revision into the canonical feature brief, complete one risk-sized analysis and design iteration, validate it, commit it, and stop
Advance this feature by exactly one development iteration without an object-oriented artifact checklist, make one coherent commit, and do not start the next iteration
Coordinate the smallest requirements, language design, and implementation work needed for one approved iteration with explicit exit evidence
Execute only the next authorized analysis/design candidate prepared by the risk-driven iteration skill, recheck its assumptions, validate it, commit once, and stop.
Run this feature with one authorized commit per iteration until the requested outcome is complete; stop only for blockers or failed validation.

negative.prompt: Select risk-driven UP analysis and design methods for this approved change without implementing it.
Design the Rust ownership transfer, staged startup rollback, async cancellation, and fallible cleanup lifecycle for this approved service behavior
Implement this bounded approved behavior from its acceptance example with a failing test first

evals.prompt: The idea at docs/ideas/session-boundary.md is approved at the current revision. Promote it into the canonical feature owner, run one question-driven design iteration suitable for the repository language, create one commit after validation, and stop.
evals.expected_output: One approved, traceable iteration updates only justified canonical owners, uses specialists selected by the actual question and language forces, validates the result, creates one authorized commit, and stops.
expectations: The accepted idea revision, one objective, non-goals, and exit evidence bound the iteration
Artifact and specialist selection follows current questions rather than a mandatory object-oriented sequence
The result stops after one scoped validated commit and names residual risk
prohibitions: Do not invent approval, product behavior, or compatibility rules
Do not require use cases, SSDs, a domain model, GRASP, realizations, and a class diagram as a fixed chain
Do not push, publish, or begin the next iteration

evals.prompt: The risk-driven analysis/design candidate E2 is separately authorized. Recheck E2 against the current repository revision, execute only that candidate, validate its exit evidence, create one commit, report assumptions that changed, and stop.
evals.expected_output: One authorized analysis/design candidate is re-baselined, executed, validated, committed once, and stopped without treating prior analysis approval as blanket execution authority.
expectations: The selected candidate's authority, source revisions, objective, dependencies, non-goals, and exit evidence are fixed before work
Stale specialist or artifact assumptions from the roadmap are corrected from current evidence while traceability is preserved
Only the selected candidate executes and the result reports whether later objectives may need replanning
At most one authorized scoped commit is created before stopping
prohibitions: Do not execute later objectives or treat prior analysis approval as blanket authority
Do not preserve a stale UP artifact checklist when the current question no longer needs it
